raw.body:
## Summary

`react-dom` enters an **infinite synchronous loop** inside the event-dispatch path — `getClosestInstanceFromNode` → `getParentHydrationBoundary` → repeated `previousSibling` walking — when:

1. the rendered tree contains an `<html>` element **nested inside a container `<div>`** (the default React Testing Library mount, under jsdom), and
2. an event is dispatched that involves portaled content with focus guards (e.g. opening a Radix UI dialog, or pointer/focus events after such content has existed in the document).

Because the loop is synchronous microtask/dispatch work, it never yields: the test runner's timeouts never fire and the process spins at 100% CPU indefinitely. Where it strikes is nondeterministic across runs (whichever event dispatch first hits the walk), which makes it look like flaky "hanging tests".

## Reproduction (18 lines, vitest + jsdom)

```tsx
import * as Dialog from "@radix-ui/react-dialog";
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

describe("nested-html repro", () => {
  it("hangs forever on the click", async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    render(
      <html lang="en">
        <body>
          <Dialog.Root>
            <Dialog.Trigger>open</Dialog.Trigger>
            <Dialog.Portal>
              <Dialog.Overlay />
              <Dialog.Content>
                <Dialog.Title>Hello</Dialog.Title>
                <button>inside</button>
              </Dialog.Content>
            </Dialog.Portal>
          </Dialog.Root>
        </body>
      </html>,
    );
    await user.click(screen.getByText("open")); // ← never returns
    expect(await screen.findByRole("dialog")).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

Remove the `<html>`/`<body>` wrapper (render the dialog directly into the container) and the same test passes in ~600 ms.

## Observed spinning stack

Captured by pausing the hung worker under the V8 inspector (`kill -USR1` + `Debugger.pause`); 100% of samples over multiple seconds sit in this loop:

```
get previousSibling
getParentHydrationBoundary        (react-dom-client.development.js)
getClosestInstanceFromNode
dispatchEventForPluginEventSystem
dispatchDiscreteEvent
[jsdom] innerInvokeEventListeners / _dispatch
fireFocusEventWithTargetAdjustment
[Radix FocusScope] focusFirst → patched focus
commitHookEffectListMount          (FocusScope's mount effect)
commitPassiveMountOnFiber
```

A related manifestation: after any render of such a nested-`<html>` tree has been mounted and unmounted, a **subsequent** `user.type()`/pointer interaction in the same jsdom document can enter the same walk via `dispatchContinuousEvent`, again never returning.

## Why this shape occurs in the wild

Frameworks whose root component renders the full document shell (`<html><head/><body>…`) — e.g. TanStack Start, and similar SSR document-root apps — hit this whenever tests mount the real root via React Testing Library's default container `<div>`. React warns `In HTML, <html> cannot be a child of <div>` (fair), but the failure mode is an unkillable synchronous hang rather than an error, and it strikes probabilistically at whichever event dispatch comes next.

**Workaround** that resolved it for us: create the root on `document` itself (`createRoot(document)`), so the rendered `<html>` becomes the real `documentElement`. It would still be worth `getParentHydrationBoundary` guarding against non-terminating walks (or React turning the invalid-nesting warning into a hard error) so the invalid case fails loudly instead of spinning forever.

## Environment

- react / react-dom **19.2.5**
- jsdom **29.1.1** (vitest **4.1.10**, `environment: "jsdom"`)
- @testing-library/react **16.3.2**, @testing-library/user-event **14.6.1**
- @radix-ui/react-dialog **1.1.15**
- node **v24.17.0**, macOS 15 (also reproduced on ubuntu-latest CI)
raw.title: Bug: infinite synchronous loop in getParentHydrationBoundary during event dispatch when <html> is rendered inside a container div (jsdom + portaled focus content)
